hints.title: Meet in the Middle Partition
hints.text: Because n is up to 40, split nums into two halves of size up to 20 to avoid 2^40 brute force.

hints.title: Generate Half Subsequence Sums
hints.text: Generate all 2^(n/2) subset sums for left half and right half, then sort the right subset sums.

hints.title: Binary Search for Complements
hints.text: For each sum in the left half, binary search in right sums to find values closest to goal minus left sum.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def minAbsDifference(self, nums: list[int], goal: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        mid = n // 2
        left_nums = nums[:mid]
        right_nums = nums[mid:]

        def get_sums(arr: list[int]) -> list[int]:
            sums = [0]
            for x in arr:
                sums += [s + x for s in sums]
            return sums

        left_sums = get_sums(left_nums)
        right_sums = sorted(get_sums(right_nums))

        ans = float('inf')
        m = len(right_sums)
        for s in left_sums:
            target = goal - s
            idx = bisect.bisect_left(right_sums, target)
            if idx < m:
                ans = min(ans, abs(s + right_sums[idx] - goal))
            if idx > 0:
                ans = min(ans, abs(s + right_sums[idx - 1] - goal))
            if ans == 0:
                return 0
        return ans
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all 2^40 subsets takes trillions of operations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Meet-in-the-middle splits 2^40 into two 2^20 sets, solvable in seconds with binary search.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate immediately identifies meet-in-the-middle technique for n around 40.
